note: Hand-curated. Every entry needs a source URL from a news outlet before it ships — scripts/suggest_openings.py surfaces candidates, a human verifies and adds them here. Dates we could not pin to a day carry a 'reported' label.

entries.name: Old Brick Store outpost (Public Service VT)
entries.area: Karma Bird House, Maple St, Burlington
entries.story: The team behind Charlotte's beloved Old Brick Store takes over the Kestrel Coffee café space at Karma Bird House — pastries, espresso, and prepared food, "the Brick on a small scale."

entries.name: Wild Meadows Books & Café
entries.dateLabel: opened early July 2026 · grand opening July 11–12
entries.story: The Williston Observer's owners opened the town's only general-interest bookstore, with local art on the walls and Mirabelles treats at the café counter.

entries.name: Nostalgia Toys & More
entries.story: The retro toy shop lasted seven months in the corner storefront that was Weenies Hot Dogs — rent, staffing, and theft made it unsustainable, the owners said.

entries.name: Feldman's Bagels
entries.story: The South End bagel shop went out of business overnight — customers found a handwritten sign on the door; the St. Albans location closed the same day.

entries.name: Burl's Downtown Kitchenette
entries.story: The Farmhouse Group turned the 1954 Oasis diner car into an all-day Southern-leaning diner — biscuits and gravy, fried chicken and waffles, patty melts, a full bar.

entries.name: The Harborvale
entries.story: The former Courtyard by Marriott reopened as a 161-room Autograph Collection hotel from the Hotel Vermont team, with chef Doug Paine's Lake Champlain-focused restaurant.

entries.name: El Cortijo Taqueria
entries.story: After 15 years the Farmhouse Group's taqueria served its last tacos in the Bank Street diner car, making way for Burl's Downtown Kitchenette.

entries.name: Small Dog Electronics (retail store)
entries.story: The region's only approved Apple repair-and-resell shop closed its Burlington storefront and moved the business online.

entries.name: Kestrel Coffee Roasters (Pine St)
entries.story: The Pine Street café poured its last shots mid-April — "all good things evolve," the owners said; their other locations stayed open.

entries.name: Dear Lucy
entries.story: The longtime Church Street shoe store closed its doors, its owner saying retail — and downtown — had changed.

entries.name: Pascolo Ristorante
entries.story: The Italian spot moved back into its original subterranean home at 83 Church Street after three years up the block — same menu, same staff.

entries.name: Mountain Valley Indian Cuisine
entries.story: The couple behind Winooski's Mountain Valley Restaurant brought their tandoori, curries, and hand-pleated momos to a former Domino's on Farrell Street.
